answer: Each agent carries a cryptographic beacon that logs its join timestamp in a publicly verifiable ledger. New recruits must present a velvet‑soft proof of work that spirals from the recruiter’s beacon, chaining signatures so any duplicate identity quickly breaks the hash chain and is rejected. An attacker must expend fresh proof‑of‑work for every fake node, turning a Sybil burst into a linear cost equal to the number of identities created.
